title: Function-routing collision in tool calls across batched requests and model aliasing
creator: Marco Silva
description: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported sporadic misrouting of tool/function calls when requests are sent in batches and the model variant uses aliasing/compatibility layers. Symptoms: correct function schema is returned in the model output but our router selects a different tool (typically an older alias), causing incorrect function invocation and downstream structured-output parsing failures. Failures are intermittent and more common under high-concurrency bursts and when customers use model alias pins (eg. model-vX -> model-vX-compat).
reproduction_steps: 1) Create two tool specs with overlapping signatures: 'parse_order_v1' and 'parse_order_v2' where v2 is a superset.
2) Configure a model alias that routes 'model-stable' -> 'model-v2-compat'.
3) Send batched requests (N=8-32) containing a mix of prompts that expect v1 and v2 behaviours simultaneously.
4) Observe function name selected in router vs function name emitted in model tools field and compare invoked function implementation.
5) Reproduce more reliably under Dedicated with reserved capacity or Private in high-concurrency customer environment (reports show higher frequency there).
logs_and_observations: A. Router metric spikes show simultaneous routing decisions within same kernel tick where request->tool mapping table snapshot is stale for a subset of inflight requests.
B. KV cache hits are identical for affected requests, suggesting the kernel selected a cached routing decision instead of recalculating per-request alias resolution.
C. In Hosted cases we see additional proxy layer de-duplication that batches alias resolution calls, correlating with timing windows where collisions happen.
D. No evidence of model output corruption; model -> tools JSON is correct, mismatch occurs between tools JSON and invocation target.
E. Error rate correlates to burst size and to presence of alias compatibility mappings; customers not using aliasing see no failures.
temporary_mitigation: 1) Instruct impacted customers to disable model aliasing and pin directly to explicit model revision (workaround: pin to model-v2 revision).
2) Reduce per-worker batch-slice size to avoid multi-tenant in-flight grouping (config change in Dedicated/private nodes).
3) Roll an emergency router configuration that forces per-request alias resolution (latency impact expected) for affected tenants.
impact: Customers experience incorrect function invocation causing downstream structured-output parsing errors, bad business logic (eg. incorrect order processing), and occasional data leakage when tools have overlapping side effects. Several customers have opened escalations to CS and engineering with production incidents and rollback asks.
root_cause_summary: Race condition in the routing layer where alias resolution state was cached per-worker tick rather than per-request when batched request windows include mixed alias contexts. Combined with a batched de-duplication optimization in the hosted proxy, the router occasionally reuses an outdated target mapping for a request that was assigned to a different slot in the batch.
timeline: 2026-02-18: First customer ticket opened (hosted) reporting unexpected function name invoked; mitigations applied (pin to revision) by SEs.
2026-02-19: Similar report from Dedicated customer with reserved capacity; on-call collected traces.
2026-02-20: Issue triaged and ENG-90412 created. Initial hypothesis recorded.
2026-02-22: Reproduced in lab using Dedicated repro harness with batch size 16; confirmed routing mismatch.
2026-02-25: Hotfix branching discussion; opted for conservative fix that updates routing snapshot boundaries.
2026-03-01: PR #op/eng/1234 created with two changes: per-request alias resolution fallback and stronger cache invalidation on alias update.
2026-03-03: Canary rollout to non-critical tenants in Hosted; observed significant drop in mismatch events but +3-6ms median latency.
2026-03-05: Rollout scheduled for Dedicated/Private after performance regression review; incident report drafted.
decisions: A. Short-term: implement per-request alias resolution fallback (safer) and conservative cache invalidation on alias updates. Trade-off: small latency increase for correctness.

B. Medium-term: redesign alias resolution to be immutable per-request context before batching decisions (larger refactor across router and batcher). Trade-off: development time and risk to batching throughput.
C. Avoided: simply disabling batching globally due to unacceptable cost and latency impact for majority of customers.
code_changes_and_prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234 - router: per-request alias fallback + cache TTL change
https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1250 - tests: deterministic repro harness for aliasing/batching
https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/78 - config: new tenant flag to opt-out of alias-batching optimization
runbook_and_rollout_notes: Runbook: tools-routing-rollback.md (Confluence) outlines steps to revert new router behaviour and to pin tenants to explicit model revisions.
Canary plan: 2% hosted tenants (non-critical), then 10% after 24h, monitor 'tool-invocation-mismatch' metric and median latency.
follow_up_tasks: 1) ENG: complete medium-term refactor for deterministic per-request alias snapshotting (estimate 13 points) - follow-up ticket.
2) QA: expand fuzz tests to include alias mappings with overlapping tool signatures and larger batch sizes.
3) PM: communicate incident note to affected customers and update status page with mitigation timeline.
4) Docs: update migration guide for Dedicated/Private customers to recommend explicit model pins for critical tooling until fix fully rolled out.
linked_artifacts: Customer ticket examples: HOSTED-1129, DED-4310, PRIVATE-221
notes: Engineering-ops will monitor after full rollout for 72h and collect customer repros for any residual failures.
Risk: customers with strict latency SLOs may object to temporary latency regression; sales/CS have been notified and offered compensation discussions.

This ticket surfaces a larger design tension between aggressive batching optimizations and per-request correctness when alias/compat mappings are used. Long-term strategy should prefer correctness for tool-calling pathways with side effects.
